worked_derivation: Maximum cash target-share count=0.5*10000=5000. In S the shortfall=5000-1000=4000; non-election priority consumes 1000, leaving 3000 cash allocations among 8000 stock elections.
S cash fraction=3000/8000=0.375; holder receives cash on 300 shares (42750) and 0.252 Broadcom shares on 500 shares (126 AVGO). V=42750+126*600=118350.
S all-in cost=800*146.50=117200; net=1150>=1000. Zero-profit AVGO price=(117200-42750)/126=590.873015873...; after fixed proration short 126 AVGO.
C fulfillment=5000/6000=5/6; 1500*(5/6)=1250 target shares receive cash (178125); remaining 250 target shares receive 63 AVGO. All C non-election shares receive stock.

For a valid stock election, the holder's stock-fulfillment fraction ranges from 1/2 (all eligible shares elect stock) to 1 (stock elections do not exceed 5000 and non-election/cash allocations satisfy cash capacity). At $600 stock consideration is $151.20>$142.50 cash. U holding 1000 receives 500 cash target shares plus 126 AVGO at the lower endpoint, or 252 AVGO at the upper endpoint, giving total-value bounds 146850 and 151200. Both bounds have feasible integer target allocations and Broadcom deliveries.
limitations: Election counts, holder positions, prices and policy thresholds are synthetic.
The supplied original agreement version is applied conditionally, not represented as a complete amended closing record.
All shares are explicitly eligible; dissenting/excluded shares, awards and tax consequences would require additional analysis.

Unknown-election bounds concern economic entitlement at a fixed supplied price before fractional-share cash conversion. They do not determine an eventual cash-in-lieu payment or constitute probability forecasts.

Whole allocated target and Broadcom share counts avoid exchange-agent fractional-rounding discretion in S/C and bound endpoints; intermediate U mixes are valued before fractional-share cash conversion.
